subfamily: rye Old-Fashioned built on one large cube; Underberg (the bitters LeNell stocked against local liquor rules) as the seasoning, sorghum syrup as the sugar
glass: small rocks glass (single old-fashioned, about 200 ml), one large ice cube
_status: v1 (Tomás, round 2), story accepted by Wren r1 (LeNell Smothers, A Proper Drink pp. 237-239). Old-Fashioned root (Codex pp. 3-6: spirit, sugar, bitters, water). Rye, when hardly anyone stocked it (Proper pp. 237, 239; Hester D5) as the style, 40-43%. Underberg named on p. 237 (recommended; substitute: any German-style herbal digestif bitters), a teaspoon in place of aromatic bitters. Sorghum syrup: Matrix pdf 240, sugar syrups pair with grain and Oxford SORGHUM pdf 1834 (pressed stalk juice, boiled); r4: tied to her 'Southern background' (p. 238) only as Tomás's choice, never 'a Southern syrup'. Matrix surprises for grain (coconut = nuts, passion fruit = OUT on acid built, clam) and for syrups (garlic, fish, olive) consulted and set aside. r3: Underberg row stays nuts (no botanical list found; Hester r2), so not veto-free.
